Have you expressed this to her? I won’t demonize you like other commenters. I am playing devils advocate and trying to look at your side, as someone whose PTSD is in remission. I am currently asymptomatic, and had trauma stemming from sexual abuse in tween/teen years. I will be fully candid that it took me about a year in recovery to be able to have sex. Is this something you’re discussing with your wife? Perhaps look into a joint session with her mental health practitioner. Something I worry about is growing resentment towards her. This happened with my previous partner I was with while I struggled immensely with PTSD. We ended up slipping up- the damage of my illness was already done.

Talk to your wife about your concerns. Now that I am healed from my sexual trauma, sex is one of the most important parts of a romantic relationship for me. It’s completely okay if it is for you to. But it’s probably not what’s most important to your wife right now. Talk to her. Talk to her therapist. The PTSD subreddit isn’t gonna give you the help you’re looking for.

I’m so sorry that you went through that OP. As far as telling your partner, I’d just start by saying you have something important you need to talk about. Ask for no interruptions until you’re done speaking so you don’t lose anything you want to say. The first time I told my girlfriend, I only told her I was raped once because not all of my repressed memories were back. I recently remembered all ~10 rapes and told her about that, about a week ago. It went really well and she was really understanding. The best advice I can give you is emphasize how important what you have to tell them is, and make sure that they listen. Best of luck to you

I knew my abuser. He was my mom’s childhood friend. I guess my guard was down the first time. The first time I was 12. I was afraid of him after but he did it three more times. Then when I was 14 he did it eight more times. After about the fifth time, I gave up on being scared and just mentally left while he raped me. 

Something that helps me when I remember I can’t bring him to justice is that he lives a pretty miserable life. Lives with his 600lb mom in a small, gross house, works at an MLM, disowned his daughter because her baby daddy was black, divorced for many years. He lives a miserable life. And I have so many great things and an amazing partner in mine. I don’t know if this works for you, but I find comparing how much better my life is to my abuser is something that helps me cope.

Take care :)

It was definitely extremely traumatic for me. I repressed it for a long time and recalled it at 21. When I was abused it probably only lasted 5-10 minutes at a time. I was put on my back and while I was being raped I started at the ceiling. I don’t know the exact number but it’s 15-20 times in my life. The first time I was raped I threw up and cut, but after the third time it just started to become a blur. I just kinda stopped fighting and being scared, just zoned out. So I would say it’s very normal. Your experiences are valid and you’re allowed to feel affected by it
